paragraphs: A Mercedes-Benz OM608 engine rebuild starts from £3,600, regardless of which of the six models it's fitted to - the price tier is set by the engine, not the badge on the boot. A full replacement engine and fitting service is also available.
Exact pricing depends on the condition of your existing engine and the parts required - submit your registration for a fixed-price quote within 30 minutes.

cards.title: Rebuilding Your
cards.body: Most engine suppliers sell you a used engine of unknown history and hope it matches. We rebuild the engine your Mercedes already has instead - strip it down, pressure-test it, and replace every worn or damaged component with updated OEM parts. You get a near-new engine with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty, without the compatibility risk of an unknown used unit. This is the option most OM608 owners choose.

cards.title: Replacement
cards.body: If your existing engine is beyond economical repair, we also offer full engine replacement and fitting - sourced and fitted by our team, with the same 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

cards.title: Used
cards.body: In some cases, a matched low-mileage used engine is the right call - particularly if you need your car back on the road quickly and your existing engine's damage is extensive. We can source and fit these too, though most owners who ask about used engines end up choosing a rebuild once they understand the compatibility risk a used unit carries.

options.body: "Reconditioned" is the term many owners search for when they mean the same thing as a rebuild - a full strip-down, inspection, and replacement of worn parts rather than a straight swap. If that's what you're after, our rebuild service is exactly that.
"Refurbished" often describes the same process from a different angle - restoring your existing engine to full working condition rather than replacing it outright. Our rebuild covers this.

Some owners specifically search for a "remanufactured" engine, expecting a unit rebuilt to original specification with updated components. That's consistent with what our rebuild service delivers, regardless of which of the six OM608-equipped models you drive.

faqLeft.q: What is the Mercedes-Benz OM608 engine?
faqLeft.a: The OM608 is Mercedes-Benz's 1.5-litre turbocharged inline-four diesel engine, in production since approximately 2014. It's fitted across two model lines - the A-Class (W177) and Citan (W420).

faqLeft.q: Which Mercedes-Benz models use the OM608?
faqLeft.a: A-Class (W177) - A 160 d, A 180 d, A 200 d - and Citan (W420) - 108 CDI through 113 variants.

faqLeft.q: Does the OM608 differ between Mercedes-Benz models?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The specific ancillaries, mounting, and vehicle-specific integration differ between passenger car and light commercial applications, even though the base engine code is the same. We match by registration/VIN before confirming any rebuild or replacement.

faqLeft.q: Is an OM608 from one Mercedes-Benz model compatible with another?
faqLeft.a: Not automatically. Ancillaries, mounting, and integration differ between the A-Class and Citan. We always confirm compatibility by registration/VIN.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes-Benz OM608 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £2,200, regardless of which model it's fitted to. Exact price depends on condition and parts required - submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.
Yes. We work on OM608 rebuilds across both the A-Class and Citan applications, replacing worn components as standard.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an OM608 from an A-Class?
faqRight.a: Yes. The OM608 in the A-Class is one of the applications we work on regularly, across the A 160 d, A 180 d, and A 200 d.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an OM608 from a Citan?
faqRight.a: Yes. The OM608 in the Citan is one of the applications we work on regularly, across the 108 CDI through 113 variants.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Mercedes-Benz OM608 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Mercedes-Benz if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes - nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an OM608 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your vehicle arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most OM608 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.
